newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower led by Samsung.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower led by Samsung.

text.p: A sharp fall in the shares of Samsung Electronics took its toll on the Seoul bourse on Friday, pushing the index to a lower close, brokers said.

Fears of further falling DRAM chip prices in the global market sparked selling in Samsung, they said. The stock hit a new year low of 56,700 won, falling 3,600 won of its limit-low. "Talk of falling chip prices sparked worries about deteriorating earnings prospects," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
The composite stock index ended 2.77 points lower at 784.37, recouping from a day low of 779.47. Despite the index fall, gainers led losers by 446 to 374 with 115 going limit up.

Brokers said investors's concerns were renewed on unconfirmed talk that the spot price for 16-megabit DRAMs had fallen below $10. "Heavy selling of Samsung Electronics shares by a local institution also dragged the share prices down," said Choi Bum of C.S. First Boston.
However, Anam Industrial Co went limit up to 12,900 after the company announced a non-memory manufacturing venture with Texas Instruments.
Profit-taking in KEPCO following sharp gains in the past two days also contributed to the index's fall. It ended at 27,300 won, unchanged from Thursday's close.

But some medium-priced large-cap shares were in demand as they have long been overlooked by investors, brokers said. Kukje hit its upper limit of 5,690 won, up 320 won and Tongil Heavy Industry also went limit up to 4,020 won, rising 220 won.
"With no sign that the economy's turning around, the market is likely to be more bearish after October. I don't expect big rises in the index this year," Choi said.
Kim of Daishin said the market would move in a boxed 760-800 range next week. The bourse later revised the index to 784.05, down 3.09 points. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
